title: Streamline GPU dependency orchestration for heterogeneous kernel fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate and simplify the runtime's GPU dependency orchestration for heterogeneous fleets (mixed CUDA versions, Triton/CUTLASS builds, and quantized kernels). The current probe-and-fallback logic is spread across multiple modules and causes transient probe jitter, duplicated symbol checks, and brittle CI gates. This ticket refactors the orchestration layer into a single lightweight dependency resolver, adds deterministic probe ordering, and introduces a compatibility score to drive safe fallbacks and targeted warmup. Goals: reduce startup probe variance, eliminate duplicated symbol resolution, and make upgrades (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS) less disruptive during image rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Single dependency-resolver module replaces at least three existing probe implementations
Probe jitter (stddev of kernel-probe latency) reduced by >= 60% on mixed-node CI matrix
No increase in end-to-end inference P95 latency in the canary cluster (<= +2%)
Canary rollout with new resolver includes automatic safe fallback to prior kernel bundle within 10 minutes on detected regressions
Unit + integration tests added to cover CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS permutations in CI matrix
comments: 2026-03-01: Spike completed — validated deterministic probe ordering is viable. Measured probe variance across 6 node types (A100v4, A100v2, H100, V100, T4, RTX6000). See benchmark notes: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gpu-probes

2026-03-04: Design review with runtime and infra — agreed to implement resolver as a thin adapter that emits a compatibility score (0-100) for kernel bundles; compatibility score will drive warmup and scheduling policy.

2026-03-06: Implemented prototype resolver and added probe cache keyed by node fingerprint. Initial results: cold-start probe latency down ~45% and fewer fallback events in local lab cluster. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892
2026-03-10: Integration test failures on CUDA 11.8 + old CUTLASS artifacts — noted missing symbol aliasing in one legacy bundle. Tracking as follow-up sub-issue ENG-271451.
2026-03-12: Running canary in eu-west-1 with 8 nodes (mixed GPUs). Metrics pipeline dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/gpu-resolver/canary-271450. No regressions observed in first 72h.
Next: finish CI matrix expansion, add rollback automation and update release notes for runtime-1.22
implementation_notes: Create 'dependency-resolver' package under runtime/infra with a stable public API used by startup, warmup, and scheduler components
Resolver will compute a compatibility score from: kernel-symbol-coverage, binary-soname-match, required-cuda-toolkit-version, and quantization-backend-compatibility
Introduce probe-cache persisted between container restarts (TTL: 24h) to reduce repeated symbol scans on autoscale events
Add feature flag 'resolver_v1' gated behind ci and canary rollout; fallback path retains legacy probe when disabled
Ensure resolver emits structured telemetry (compatibility_score, probe_latency_ms, fallback_reason) to tracer and metrics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: resolver bug could misclassify compatibility and cause silent correctness regressions. Mitigation: run canary with strict quality checks + automatic rollback if regression detected in eval-suite
Risk: persistent probe-cache might mask hardware changes after driver upgrades. Mitigation: invalidate cache on node fingerprint/driver version change
Risk: expanding CI matrix increases runtime for PRs. Mitigation: run full matrix in nightly and a curated subset per PR; use emulation for low-risk permutations
